# Urbo

Urbo is an open source smart city app platform that retrieves services and information from various
sources and makes them available on a single platform for citizens.

The app accesses data from city-specific backends and bundles the available content into thematic-functional
modules. Cities can configure which modules are active and adapt the branding to their own identity.

The available feature modules are:

- News
- Events
- Citizen services
- Feedback/Support
- Parking
- POIs
- Waste calendar
- Construction sites
- Funfair / Special events
- Citizen participation
- Surveys (LimeSurvey)
- Link lists
- Image spotlight
- NINA emergency alerts
- Here & Now (smart recommendations)
- Push notifications
- User account management (profile, account deletion)

Urbo is developed and maintained by [SWCode](https://swcode.io).

## Project status

Urbo is **actively developed** and in production. It runs as the citizen app of several German
cities, and development continues on `main` with releases cut from `app-v*` tags — at the time of
writing, several times per working day (278 `app-v2.0.x` releases since 2026-06-22, an average of
roughly 4-5 per working day).

- **Releases:** every release is an `app-v*` tag, listed at
  [gitlab.opencode.de/urbo-community/urbo/-/tags](https://gitlab.opencode.de/urbo-community/urbo/-/tags).
- **Versioning:** how the version numbers are formed and what a bump means is described in
  [docs/versioning.md](./docs/versioning.md).
- **Where it is going:** the feature modules listed above are the delivered scope. Work in
  progress and planned changes are tracked as issues and design documents under
  [docs/plans/](./docs/plans/).
- **Contributing:** see [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md). Security reports go through
  [SECURITY.md](./SECURITY.md), not the issue tracker.

# Urbo task runner. Run `just` (or `just --list`) to see all recipes.

set windows-shell := ["C:\\Program Files\\Git\\bin\\sh.exe", "-c"]

urbo := "scripts/urbo"

# List all available recipes.
default:
    @just --list

# Bring up the whole stack for this worktree: deps, infrastructure, backend, seed data, dev servers. Flags: --fresh, --detach, --no-seed, --apps=<names>, --with-limesurvey.
up *ARGS:
    node {{urbo}}/up.mjs {{ARGS}}

# Start only the dev servers against an already-running instance (what `just up --detach` skips).
serve *ARGS:
    node {{urbo}}/serve.mjs {{ARGS}}

# Wipe this instance's data and bring everything up again from scratch.
fresh:
    node {{urbo}}/up.mjs --fresh

# Stop this instance's containers, keeping its data.
down:
    node {{urbo}}/cli.mjs down

# Stop this instance and delete its volumes (database, search index, S3 objects).
reset:
    node {{urbo}}/cli.mjs reset

# Re-import this instance's Keycloak realm after a template change, keeping its seeded content.
reset-auth:
    node {{urbo}}/reset-auth.mjs

# Show the status of this instance's containers.
status:
    node {{urbo}}/cli.mjs status

# Print this instance's URLs.
urls:
    node {{urbo}}/cli.mjs urls

# Open one of this instance's URLs in the browser. Run without a target to list them.
open target="":
    node {{urbo}}/cli.mjs open {{target}}

# Follow this instance's container logs. Pass a service name to narrow it down.
logs *ARGS:
    node {{urbo}}/cli.mjs logs {{ARGS}}

# Open a shell in one of this instance's containers.
sh service:
    node {{urbo}}/cli.mjs sh {{service}}

# List every Urbo instance running on this machine, across all worktrees.
ls:
    node {{urbo}}/cli.mjs ls

# Remove Docker networks and volumes left behind by deleted instances.
prune:
    node {{urbo}}/cli.mjs prune

# Run the preflight checks on their own and print how to fix what fails.
doctor:
    node {{urbo}}/preflight.mjs

# Run the unit tests for the orchestration scripts.
test-scripts:
    node --test "scripts/urbo/*.test.mjs"

# Run the Spring Boot backend on the host against this instance's infrastructure.
backend-local:
    node {{urbo}}/backend-local.mjs

# Build the citizen app and sync it into the native project, pointed at this instance.
native platform:
    node {{urbo}}/native.mjs {{platform}}

# Regenerate the aggregated CycloneDX SBOM at the repository root.
sbom:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    mkdir -p .sbom-tmp
    trap 'rm -rf .sbom-tmp' EXIT

    cd backend && ./gradlew --quiet --no-daemon cyclonedxBom && cd ..
    cp backend/build/reports/cyclonedx/bom.json .sbom-tmp/backend.json

    # cdxgen reads license/author/description metadata straight out of each package's
    # own files under node_modules when that tree already exists, and falls back to
    # thinner lockfile-only data when it does not -- so the same command produces a
    # materially different document depending on whether `app/` happened to be
    # installed already. `--no-install-deps` does not fix this: it only controls
    # whether cdxgen installs anything itself, not whether it reads a tree that is
    # already there. Installing here, unconditionally and from the frozen lockfile,
    # makes the output depend only on pnpm-lock.yaml, never on the caller's prior state.
    cd app && pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && cd ..
    cd app && pnpm dlx @cyclonedx/cdxgen@12.8.4 --type pnpm --no-install-deps --output ../.sbom-tmp/frontend.json . && cd ..

    docker run --rm --volume "$PWD/.sbom-tmp:/work" --workdir /work \
        cyclonedx/cyclonedx-cli:0.33.1 \
        merge --input-files backend.json frontend.json --output-file merged.json

    # serialNumber, metadata.timestamp and metadata.component.bom-ref are optional in
    # CycloneDX and change on every run. cdxgen also appends a top-level `annotations`
    # entry that embeds the scan's wall-clock time in both its `timestamp` and its
    # human-readable `text` ("...created on Tuesday, September 15, 2026...") -- pure
    # generation metadata, not dependency data, so it is dropped rather than patched.
    # cdxgen additionally writes a `cdx:npm:package_json` property on local workspace
    # components whose value is the absolute filesystem path to that package's
    # package.json -- unlike the rest of `properties`, that one field is a property of
    # the checkout, not of the dependency, so it is stripped by pattern rather than by
    # name (a future generator could leak a path under a different key just as easily).
    # Stripping all of this makes the recipe idempotent across machines, which is what
    # lets CI diff the committed file against a fresh one. When it was generated is in
    # the commit.
    node -e "const fs=require('fs');
      const bom=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync('.sbom-tmp/merged.json','utf8'));
      delete bom.serialNumber;
      delete bom.annotations;
      if (bom.metadata) {
        delete bom.metadata.timestamp;
        if (bom.metadata.component) delete bom.metadata.component['bom-ref'];
      }
      const isLocalPath = (v) => typeof v === 'string' && /^\/(Users|home)\/|^\/private\//.test(v);
      for (const component of bom.components || []) {
        if (!component.properties) continue;
        component.properties = component.properties.filter((p) => !isLocalPath(p.value));
        if (component.properties.length === 0) delete component.properties;
      }
      fs.writeFileSync('sbom.cdx.json', JSON.stringify(bom, null, 2) + '\n');"

# Local development only — builds the JAR inside Docker so no local JDK is required.
# Production image: ../../Dockerfile (expects a pre-built JAR from CI).
# If the base image or JVM flags in the production Dockerfile change, update this file too.

FROM eclipse-temurin:25-jdk-alpine AS build

WORKDIR /workspace/app
COPY . .
# sharing=locked: two instances building at the same time must not write this cache concurrently.
# The registry token arrives as a BuildKit secret, mounted only for this RUN: an ARG/ENV would
# persist it in the image layer, where `docker history` can read it back.
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.gradle,sharing=locked \
    --mount=type=secret,id=github_token \
    chmod +x ./gradlew \
    && GITHUB_TOKEN="$(cat /run/secrets/github_token)" ./gradlew bootJar

FROM amazoncorretto:25

EXPOSE 8080

COPY --from=build /workspace/app/urbo-app/build/libs/urbo-app.jar /app.jar

ENV SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE=local
